reasoning: Lane: industry. DY fell from $566 (May) to $179 as the market moved from AI/data-center enthusiasm to an FTTH down-cycle: Q2 Comms margin -134bp and $150M wireless deferral (Aug), then the Q3 warning that several large customers will slow FTTH builds in 2027 (FY2028 FTTH down, Comms mid-single-digit). The chain confirms the slowdown: AT&T cut 2027-28 capex ~$1B/yr while keeping 60M locations by 2030; MasTec's Communications fell 11.8% with customer deferrals; Shentel ends its expansion in 2026; two DY customers defaulted. It also confirms the offsets: Zayo's 8,000-route-mile AI-anchored long-haul program and doubled long-haul dark-fiber demand, Corning's multi-billion carrier fiber contracts (AT&T, Verizon), all 56 BEAD final proposals approved, AT&T copper retirement milestones through 2029, and AI data-center capex +50% in 2027 (standing view) for Building Systems. Build: core Comms -4% in FY2028 (below the CEO's mid-single-digit total), long-haul 250->650->1,000, Building Systems +18%/+14%, Comms EBITA held ~9.5-9.8%, BS 18%/17.5%; FY2028 adj. EPS ~$19.3 (4% below the pre-print Zacks $20.11), FY2029 ~$22.4. Valuation: P/E 11.2x (peer median 16.0x shrunk at k=0.8 from DY's 10.2x) and EV/EBITDA 8.2x cross-check -> $257 base. The base is well above spot because the k-rule keeps only part of a discount that sits at a cyclical extreme; moderately conservative drivers (rule 0c) are used to offset this. P10 $131: deeper FTTH cuts, slower long-haul, BS margin back toward mid-teens, P/E -2.5 turns (about -27% from spot, matching a 59%-vol name's 1-in-10). P90 $409: BEAD/copper/long-haul fill the FTTH hole, BS margins hold near Q3, re-rating toward peers. Research was limited: SEC press-release exhibits for Q1/Q2 FY2027 segment data could not be fetched (folder fetch failed), the MasTec call recap was blocked, and consensus feeds are pre-print. 13 of 24 sources are in lane; most of the rest are the company's own basics (filings, release, call) and the consensus feeds.

model_inputs.structure_note: Two-segment driver build (Communications = core FTTH/maintenance/wireless/copper/BEAD + long-haul/DCI; Building Systems = data-center electrical + structured cabling), 3 fiscal years FY2027-FY2029 (FY ends late January). Value carried by a P/E horizon leg (0.75) on the build's own NTM adjusted EPS (ex amortization of acquired intangibles, SBC costed) and a mid-cycle EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25) on NTM adjusted EBITDA. EBIT here is EBITA before SBC (adjusted EBITDA less depreciation); the engine deducts SBC (sbc_treatment cost). No DCF (engine policy). Leg weights are judgment, untested.
model_inputs.gap_note: Annual (not quarterly) driver set: built by a forecaster for comparison; the supervisor's reconciled set should be quarterly. FY2026 base split of long-haul vs core Communications is not disclosed: long-haul base $150M is an estimate from the CEO's 'several hundred million dollars of work in place over the past 2 years' (low confidence). Consensus on the feeds is pre-print (Zacks Q3 est. $4.56 vs $5.23 actual; FY2028 $20.11 assumes no FTTH decline); the own NTM P/E of 10.2x will rise when the street cuts FY2028, which would lift the k=0.8 exit multiple (variant: own 11x -> exit 11.9x, about +5%). Playbook trap: DY may use supplier-finance/factoring; not found in the fact pack and not added to net debt; DSO 112 days. Amortization of acquired intangibles (~$59.5M a quarter, F-lookup AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets) is excluded from the P/E basis on the peers' adjusted basis; GAAP EPS runs ~$5-6 below. Other non-operating expense (~$10M a year, F86/F87) is not in the engine EPS (about -$0.25/share). EV/EBITDA leg uses a trailing peer median against forward EBITDA (conservative). Judgment calls for Kilian: FY2028 Communications growth 2.5% vs the CEO's mid-single digit (engine: at +5% the target rises ~4%); Building Systems FY2028 EBITA 18% vs Q3's ~22.8%.
